newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rate cut possible in few months - Belka.
newsitem.headline: Polish rate cut possible in few months - Belka.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is likely to lower official interest rates in several months or in the second half of the year, Finance Minister Marek Belka said.
Belka also said on Thursday that presently the central bank was justified in keeping real interest rates rising to curb import-boosting domestic demand and keep the widening trade deficit in check.

"A real interest rate rise, which is happening because nominal rates are not being lowered, is justified...but later in the year, in the second half or in several months (official interest rate) cuts could take place, should take place and probably will take place," Belka told public radio.

Belka said on Wednesday fighting the growing trade gap was a higher priority than curbing inflation this year and this called for a tight monetary policy and not slowing the zloty's devaluation rate even at the cost of higher price growth.
Poland's current account trade gap widened to $8.2 billion last year from a $1.8 billion shortfall in 1995.
The government's official trade deficit target for 1997 was set at $12 billion, but many analysts said this figure was likely to be surpassed.

The independent central bank increased banks' obligatory reserves at the end of February to slow troublesome growth of credit to households but has kept official interest rates flat at 22 and 25 percent since mid-1996.
